If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for pessimism.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, shift forecast peak to later horizon (16–30 days) and reduce slope steepness to reflect delayed market reaction.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows upward trend, cap upward movement at +1.0% for late horizon (21–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is high but forecast is flat or declining, add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast for early horizon to align with sentiment-driven volatility.

If sentiment is low but forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid horizon to reflect sentiment-driven reversal risk.
